code_switch_mapping_method: Recomputed with explicit exclusive-leaning Cebuano, Tagalog, and English marker lexicons; markers and assigned type are recorded row by row in code_switch_marker_evidence_by_case_id. This is an assistive lexical audit, not a fluent-human language identification. Uncertain cases are retained as unclear_requires_human_language_review, not forced into a category.
rubric_version_reference: TEXT-RUBRIC-0.2-B; all proposed labels remain drafts and require accountable human approval.
source: AI-authored synthetic mixed Cebuano-English, Tagalog-English, Cebuano-Tagalog, and tri-language road/vehicle report drafts.
limitations: All rows are synthetic and are not observed civilian reports or responder-confirmed ground truth.
Labels are proposed drafts; reviewers must assess exact text under TEXT-RUBRIC-0.2-B.
Code-switch classifications are lexical-heuristic indicators and require fluent Cebuano and Tagalog confirmation.
No training, evaluation, calibration, active-model update, or deployment was performed.
Scenario-family and annotation-group IDs intentionally link the documented near-paraphrase rows; those links are listed below and do not assert human approval.

family_link_review.rationale: Two near-paraphrases describe the same serious leg-wound-after-crash scenario; the variant inherits the base family and group.
